title: Formalizing and Mitigating Structural Distortion in LLM Attention for Graph Reasoning

problem.claim: Linearizing graph structure into sequences introduces structural distortion in LLM-based graph reasoning.

gap.claim: The mechanism underlying distortion-related performance degradation is unclear because it is often attributed to prompt design or model scale.

contributions.claim: The paper explains graph linearization as bandwidth-dependent attention decay caused by rotary positional embeddings.
The paper proposes Graph-aligned Language Attention (GaLA), a lightweight inference-time modification that biases attention toward graph-adjacent nodes while preserving sequential inductive biases.
The paper reports that GaLA improves performance across Text-Attributed Graph benchmarks with low overhead.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GaLA improves performance across Text-Attributed Graph benchmarks with low overhead.
The authors report that structural distortion is a correctable bottleneck in LLM-based graph reasoning.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs show promise for reasoning over Text-Attributed Graphs.
Graph linearization introduces distortion related to the graph bandwidth problem, and its mechanism is unclear.
Rotary positional embeddings are described as causing bandwidth-dependent attention decay between graph-adjacent nodes placed far apart in the serialized sequence.
The authors shift attention toward correcting attention misalignment and propose GaLA to bias attention toward graph-adjacent nodes.
The authors report improved benchmark performance with low overhead and characterize distortion as a correctable bottleneck.

source_observation.claim: Serialization can weaken attention between related graph elements when graph adjacency and sequence distance diverge.

interpretation.claim: For graph reasoning with sequence-based models, representational alignment may be a distinct bottleneck from prompt quality or model scale.

application.claim: Inference-time attention biases could be used to preserve graph-local relationships without replacing the underlying sequential model.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported Text-Attributed Graph benchmarks or graph serialization settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated benchmarks, models, datasets, baselines, or quantitative performance improvements.
The abstract does not provide the exact GaLA formulation, overhead measurements, or implementation details.
The abstract does not report limitations, failure cases, or independent verification.
